correctness.rationale: For n≥4 the wheel has diameter two. A hub-free subset is in general position exactly when it contains no run of three consecutive selected rim vertices, and a subset containing the hub must have a rim clique. Thus the complex is the two-independence complex of the rim with a disk attached along the rim cycle. At n=3 the graph is complete. At n=4 the disk together with the two diagonals is the entire complex; collapsing the contractible disk as a subcomplex gives a bouquet of two circles. At n=5 the rim-only triangles are precisely {i,i+1,i+3} modulo five, and the other triangles are the five hub triangles. The hub link is C_5 and the rim-vertex 0 link, in cyclic order, is h,1,3,2,4,h; symmetry covers all rim links. There are 6 vertices, 15 edges, 10 triangles, no larger faces, and the links give a closed connected surface of Euler characteristic 1, hence a projective plane. One can also obtain integral H_1 by contracting the hub spokes as a spanning tree and using the hub triangles to kill the rim edges: the oriented diagonals D_i=(i,i+2) then satisfy D_{i+1}+D_{i+3}=0 around an odd cycle, giving Z/2. For n≥6 we checked the actual cycle homotopy theorem (Deshpande–Singh, Thm. 4.6 with d=4); each sphere in its stated specialization has dimension ≥2. The attaching loop is null and the cofibration splits up to homotopy, giving precisely the asserted additional S². The result and its integral torsion assertion are correct; the frozen verifier's finite mod-two tests are not an all-size or integral proof.
